_description: One row per key phrase or language pattern extracted from a process-signal filing. A single filing event generates 2–15 language observations. This table calibrates item4_parser phrase weights, downgrade marker effectiveness, and boilerplate detection. It is the most granular layer and enables direct language-to-outcome analysis.

filing_date.description: Date of the source filing. Redundant with event_id for query convenience.

phrase.description: The exact phrase as it appears in the filing text. Verbatim. No paraphrasing.

phrase_category.description: Semantic category of the phrase. Used to validate and refine item4_parser bucket assignments.

surrounding_context.description: 50–100 words of surrounding context from the filing. Critical for evaluating whether isolated phrase match is legitimate or misleading.

section_source.description: Which section of the filing this phrase came from. Item 4 language is structurally different from body or risk-factor language.

raw_weight_assigned.description: Numeric weight item4_parser would assign to this phrase (0–100). Null if not parseable or not applicable.

is_downgrade_marker.description: True if this phrase is a hedging or downgrade marker (e.g., 'no assurance', 'from time to time', 'may consider'). Used to calibrate hedge_factor logic in item4_parser.

downgrade_severity.description: Subjective strength of the downgrade hedge. STRONG = nearly eliminates signal. WEAK = minor qualification.

classification_at_time.description: How item4_parser would classify this phrase's contribution. Derived from bucket assignment, not from outcome.

is_sale_pressure.description: True if this phrase alone contributes to is_sale_pressure=True classification in item4_parser.

confidence_score.description: item4_parser confidence_score for the filing this phrase came from (0–100). Same value for all phrases from the same filing.

later_outcome.description: What eventually happened to this case. Filled retrospectively. Never fill during initial labeling.

phrase_was_predictive.description: Retrospective label: did this phrase type appear in cases that resolved with a deal? Used to validate phrase-weight calibration. Never fill during initial labeling.

notes.description: Anything unusual about this phrase or context — ambiguous meaning, possible boilerplate, unusual phrasing.

_calibration_notes.phrase_weight_validation: Compare raw_weight_assigned distribution across later_outcome=ACQUIRED vs later_outcome=DEAL_FAILED. If high-weight phrases do not correlate with better outcomes, recalibrate bucket weights in item4_parser.
_calibration_notes.downgrade_marker_validation: Compare cases with many is_downgrade_marker=True observations against outcome. If downgrade-heavy filings have similar P(deal) to low-hedge filings, reduce hedge_factor strength.
_calibration_notes.boilerplate_detection: Phrases labeled BOILERPLATE that appear in later_outcome=ACQUIRED cases flag potential over-suppression. Review if BOILERPLATE classification is too aggressive.
_calibration_notes.minimum_for_calibration: Minimum 500 language observations from minimum 80 VERIFIED cases before any phrase-weight recalibration.
